exposure: deviation from normal progress during labour
incidence of complications among similar labours
cohort: The study utilized data from 9,995 women admitted for labour in 2014-2015 in thirteen major regional health care facilities across Nigeria and Uganda.
finding: The proposed machine-learning approach for real-time labour monitoring and decision support yielded sensitivity and specificity of approximately 0.70 for caesarean section prediction, outperforming the partograph and matching the performance of state-of-the-art supervised machine-learning models while offering superior flexibility and interpretability.
mod_finding: The study's primary finding relates to the prediction of caesarean section, a mode of birth, demonstrating that the new machine learning model is more effective than traditional methods for this outcome.
